methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Emelody is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jon Thomas and Elizabeth Johnson that has raised $10M+. The valuation universe comprises 10 peers in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including eight private companies (Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics among them) and one public comparable (277810.KQ).

Stage-Progression methodology is applicable and provides the primary valuation signal. Using total raised ($10M) as a proxy baseline and applying a typical 1.2x step-up multiplier for progression within the Growth stage yields an implied valuation of $12M. Peer-Median triangulation was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum data thresholds; a broader sectoral median would introduce excessive noise without meaningful narrowing.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This range reflects ceiling and floor bounds derived from the Stage-Progression methodology applied conservatively. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight-fitting peer multiples within Emelody's specific valuation tier and stage, which limits confidence in cross-sectional anchoring. Revenue metrics, growth rate, and capital efficiency ratios—unavailable in the current dataset—would materially refine this estimate and warrant collection in follow-up diligence.
